:::{#thm-epe-decomposition}
#### Bias, variance and noise

Let $\mean$ be the [mean function](#def-mean-function) of the outcome given the covariate.
Suppose that, given $\newpredvar = \predvar$,
the new outcome is $\newoutvar = \mean(\predvar) + \noise$,
where $\noise$, the noise in the outcome at $\predvar$, has mean $0$ and variance $\varpar$,
and that $\newoutvar$ is independent of the random training set $\trainset$,
and that $\E{\fitproc\paren{\predvar; \trainset}^2} < \infty$.
Then the [expected squared prediction error at $\predvar$](#def-epe)
is the squared [bias](#def-prediction-bias)
of the prediction $\fitproc\paren{\predvar; \trainset}$ as a prediction of $\mean(\predvar)$,
plus its [variance](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/variance-covariance.html#def-variance),
plus $\varpar$:

$$
\epe{\fitproc}{\nobs}{\predvar} = \sqf{\bias{\fitproc\paren{\predvar; \trainset}}}
+ \Var{\fitproc\paren{\predvar; \trainset}} + \varpar.
$$ {#eq-epe-decomposition}

:::

::: proof

Write $\targeterrf{\predvar} \eqdef \mean(\predvar) - \fitproc\paren{\predvar; \trainset}$,
the error of the prediction as an estimate of $\mean(\predvar)$.
Given $\newpredvar = \predvar$, the noise has mean 0 by @eq-mean-function and variance $\varpar$,
and it is independent of $\fitproc\paren{\predvar; \trainset}$
because $\newoutvar$ is independent of $\trainset$;
hence it is independent of $\targeterrf{\predvar}$,
because $\mean(\predvar)$ is a constant.

First, the prediction error in terms of $\noise$ and $\targeterrf{\predvar}$:

$$
\ba
\newoutvar - \fitproc\paren{\predvar; \trainset}
&= \paren{\mean(\predvar) + \noise} - \fitproc\paren{\predvar; \trainset}
&& \text{(definition of } \newoutvar \text{)} \\
&= \noise + \paren{\mean(\predvar) - \fitproc\paren{\predvar; \trainset}}
&& \text{(reorder the terms of the sum)} \\
&= \noise + \targeterrf{\predvar}
&& \text{(definition of } \targeterrf{\predvar} \text{)}
\ea
$$

Next, expand the square and split the expectation.
The first line is the definition of the expected squared prediction error at $\predvar$,
which conditions on $\newpredvar = \predvar$;
all expectations in the lines after it are conditional on $\newpredvar = \predvar$ too.
The last two steps use
[linearity of expectation](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/expectation.html#thm-linearity-expectation),
first for the expectation of a sum and then for a constant factor:

$$
\ba
\epe{\fitproc}{\nobs}{\predvar}
&= \E{\sqf{\noise + \targeterrf{\predvar}} \mid \newpredvar = \predvar}
&& \text{(definition and the error above)} \\
&= \E{\noise^2 + 2 \noise \targeterrf{\predvar} + \sqf{\targeterrf{\predvar}}}
&& \text{(expand the square of a sum)} \\
&= \E{\noise^2} + \E{2 \noise \targeterrf{\predvar}} + \E{\sqf{\targeterrf{\predvar}}}
&& \text{(expectation of a sum)} \\
&= \E{\noise^2} + 2\E{\noise \targeterrf{\predvar}} + \E{\sqf{\targeterrf{\predvar}}}
&& \text{(constant factor 2)}
\ea
$$

Each of the three terms is evaluated in turn.

- For the noise term, the
  [variance identity](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/variance-covariance.html#thm-variance)
  gives $\varpar = \E{\noise^2} - \sqf{\E{\noise}}$,
  and $\E{\noise} = 0$, so $\E{\noise^2} = \varpar$.
- For the cross term,
  $\noise$ is independent of $\targeterrf{\predvar}$,
  so the expectation of the product is the product of the expectations:

  $$
  \ba
  \E{\noise \targeterrf{\predvar}}
  &= \E{\noise}\E{\targeterrf{\predvar}}
  && \text{(independence)} \\
  &= 0 \cdot \E{\targeterrf{\predvar}}
  && \text{(} \E{\noise} = 0 \text{)} \\
  &= 0
  && \text{(zero times a number)}
  \ea
  $$

- For the last term,
  the variance identity gives
  $\E{\sqf{\targeterrf{\predvar}}} = \Var{\targeterrf{\predvar}} + \sqf{\E{\targeterrf{\predvar}}}$.
  The mean of $\targeterrf{\predvar}$ is

  $$
  \ba
  \E{\targeterrf{\predvar}}
  &= \E{\mean(\predvar)} - \E{\fitproc\paren{\predvar; \trainset}}
  && \text{(expectation of a difference)} \\
  &= \mean(\predvar) - \E{\fitproc\paren{\predvar; \trainset}}
  && \text{(} \mean(\predvar) \text{ is a constant)} \\
  &= -\paren{\E{\fitproc\paren{\predvar; \trainset}} - \mean(\predvar)}
  && \text{(factor out } -1 \text{)} \\
  &= -\bias{\fitproc\paren{\predvar; \trainset}}
  && \text{(definition of bias)}
  \ea
  $$

  so $\sqf{\E{\targeterrf{\predvar}}} = \sqf{\bias{\fitproc\paren{\predvar; \trainset}}}$,
  because a number and its negative have the same square.
  The variance of $\targeterrf{\predvar}$ is

  $$
  \ba
  \Var{\targeterrf{\predvar}}
  &= \E{\sqf{\targeterrf{\predvar} - \E{\targeterrf{\predvar}}}}
  && \text{(definition of variance)} \\
  &= \E{\sqf{-\paren{\fitproc\paren{\predvar; \trainset} - \E{\fitproc\paren{\predvar; \trainset}}}}}
  && \text{(substitute; the constant } \mean(\predvar) \text{ cancels)} \\
  &= \E{\sqf{\fitproc\paren{\predvar; \trainset} - \E{\fitproc\paren{\predvar; \trainset}}}}
  && \text{(a number and its negative have the same square)} \\
  &= \Var{\fitproc\paren{\predvar; \trainset}}
  && \text{(definition of variance)}
  \ea
  $$

Substituting the three terms into the expansion gives

$$
\ba
\epe{\fitproc}{\nobs}{\predvar}
&= \varpar + 2 \cdot 0 + \paren{\Var{\fitproc\paren{\predvar; \trainset}} + \sqf{\bias{\fitproc\paren{\predvar; \trainset}}}}
&& \text{(the three terms above)} \\
&= \sqf{\bias{\fitproc\paren{\predvar; \trainset}}} + \Var{\fitproc\paren{\predvar; \trainset}} + \varpar
&& \text{(drop } 2 \cdot 0 \text{, reorder the terms)}
\ea
$$

:::
